title: Three port names are malformed in the frontend's port-of-entry list — a misspelt Teesport, a shouted TILBURY and a Portsmouth Port with a doubled space — where DR1 spells every port in ordinary sentence case.

finding.frontend: Three of the seventy-eight ports a user can pick are written wrong. GB TEE is named "Teestort", which is not a place — Teesport is (src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:302-305). GB TIL is named "TILBURY" in capitals, sitting on the same list as "Tilbury Port" and "Tilbury 2 Ro-Ro Terminal" in ordinary case (:294-297). GB PME is named "Portsmouth  Port" with two spaces between the words (:266-269). The misspelling is the one that costs a user something: the search matches on the text as written, so typing "Teesport" returns nothing and the port looks absent from the service.
finding.prototype: DR1's catalogue spells two of the same places properly and in ordinary case — Teesport (app/data/uk-airports.js:186) and Tilbury (:189). It has no Portsmouth entry at all, so DR1 takes no position on that third name.
finding.difference: Correct the three names in the reference-data port catalogue: Teestort to Teesport, TILBURY to title case, and the doubled space in Portsmouth Port to one. The codes do not change, so nothing already submitted is affected. The list reaches the frontend from the reference-data service and is only captured into the repo as a fixture, so the correction lands upstream and the fixture is recaptured after it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding that GB TEE is officially registered as "Teestort" rather than Teesport in the UN/LOCODE data the reference-data service draws on.
finding.correction: CLAIMED: three frontend port names are malformed where DR1 spells all three properly. ALL THREE FRONTEND DEFECTS CONFIRMED IN THE CAPTURED DOM, not just in source: the port control renders 'Teestort (GB TEE)', 'TILBURY (GB TIL)' and 'Portsmouth  Port (GB PME)' with the doubled space intact (capture/html/frontend/fe-arrival-details.html; fixture at src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:294-297, 302-305, 266-269). MIS-CITED, slot corrected: the prototype leg cited app/data/uk-airports.js:186-189 for all three names. Those four lines are Teesport, Teignmouth, Thamesport and Tilbury — DR1 has no Portsmouth entry anywhere in the file. So two of the three have a DR1 comparator and the third does not; the doubled space is still a defect in the frontend's own catalogue but it is not a parity difference, and whoever writes the ticket should say so. The Teesport misspelling is the one that costs a user something and it is unambiguous — the control matches on the text as written, so typing 'Teesport' returns nothing. BAND CONFIRMED FROM A REAL DEPENDENCY: the catalogue is fetched from the reference-data service at /ports-of-entry (src/server/app/services/ports/client.js) and only captured into the repo as a fixture, so the correction lands upstream and the fixture is recaptured after it. TWO FINDINGS OR ONE, with the duplicates finding: two, and they no longer travel together — the duplicates finding has been disputed because DR1 repeats port names itself, so this one now stands alone.

relatedTo.why: Both are defects in the same reference-data port catalogue and would be fixed in one pass
